We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We must produce JSON route where each reaction node uses the given template_id (as integer? example shows number). The route must start from target molecule (given SMILES). Then apply first template 29646 to get precursors, then each subsequent reaction on each precursor? Typically linear route: each reaction transforms one molecule into precursors, then further reactions on those precursors. Need at least 5 reactions total, using those templates in order.

We attempted applying 29646 gave three possible precursors (list). The result from apply_template gave three tuples: each tuple seems to be a set of precursors? The result format: "(('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)',))"

Looks like three possible outcomes each with one precursor? Actually each tuple contains a single SMILES. So template 29646 likely a protecting group removal? Not sure.

We need to construct a route using these templates. Perhaps we can choose one of the precursors to continue.

We need to apply template 1914389 to the product of previous step? Actually order: 29646 then 1914389 then 1914390 then 149040 then 1914391.

Thus after first reaction (29646) we get a precursor (choose one). Then apply 1914389 to that precursor to get its precursors, etc.

We need to find applicable matches. We attempted applying 1914389 to some molecules; got results for some but not others.

We got a successful application of 1914389 to "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" gave two precursors: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" and "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". Good.

So we can choose that as second step.

Now apply 1914390 to the first precursor "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO". We attempted earlier and got empty result. So maybe need to apply 1914390 to the second precursor "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". That also gave empty.

Maybe we need to apply 1914390 to a different molecule. Could be that template 1914390 expects a protected group? Not sure.

We could try applying 149040 to something later.

But perhaps we can construct a route where each reaction uses the template but some steps may have no precursors (i.e., template not applicable) - but route must be valid? Probably need each step to produce precursors.

We may need to search for templates applicability. Could use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching to verify.

Let's try check for 1914390 on the first precursor.
